properties.description:
BUILT 2026-10-10 (reflow2 PR #714, feat/every-served-tool-carries-a-title, commit 0c5058f43). Every #[tool] attribute in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/*.rs, and the latent and degraded servers' tools, carries rmcp's `title` (Title Case, two to six words, derived from the tool's name and its first sentence, consistent across families: every add_* "Add a …", every *_report "… Report"); every tool whose annotations say read_only_hint = false carries destructive_hint. Measured on the branch binary: 197 tools, 197 titled, 119 writers, 119 with destructiveHint; on main 197 / 0 / 119 / 7.
destructiveHint = true on seven: delete_node, delete_edge, apply_heal (its merge deletes a node, no undo), import_graph (upsert overwrites existing ids), apply_merge (merge.rs removes nodes and edges one side deleted), contain_component and move_component (both detach existing parents). The rest are false: they add, or revise with the prior state preserved.
ONE CORRECTION, NOT ADDITIVE: apply_merge said destructive_hint = false on main and now says true, because merge.rs removes nodes and edges. Flagged for Anthony; a one-line revert if he disagrees.
NOT CHANGED, deliberately: export_graph and export_surface overwrite a file, but they are read_only_hint = true and MCP makes destructiveHint meaningful only on writers; flipping readOnlyHint would reclassify them as writes (refused while a server holds the graph) and break the surface-only-grows rule. The latent and degraded servers' tools got titles and no annotations, as before. The toolsnap goldens were re-blessed (diff: title and destructiveHint only); the surface fixture at the last release was untouched (it compares readOnlyHint and schemas only).
Additive on the wire otherwise: no tool name, argument, description or reply changed; readOnlyHint unchanged on all 197. flo2.io serves about 187 of these (it withholds the file-opening tools), so the Claude Connectors Directory sees the titled subset.
properties.name: Every served tool carries a title, and every writing tool says whether it can destroy
